hook_text: 32 out of 50 people said they would pay for your idea. Is that enough to start a business?
clip_script: Meet Shine on Wheels, a mobile car wash. Before spending a cent, the owner does a SWOT. Strengths: comes to you, R30 cheaper than the filling station, uses 20 litres instead of 150. Weaknesses: little money, no name yet. Opportunities: office parks full of parked cars, and 32 out of 50 people surveyed said yes. That is 64 percent. Threats: water restrictions, crime, a price war. Now the clever part. Mix them. Strength plus opportunity: wash cars while people work. Strength against threat: so little water that restrictions barely matter. That threat just became a selling point. Then describe the product: not the best wash ever, but a R120 wash at your office in 40 minutes. Features tell. Benefits sell.
visual_style: A four-block SWOT grid filling in with icons, arrows linking strengths to opportunities, a water drop shrinking from 150 to 20 litres.
pacing: Quick hook with the survey number, fast-filled grid, one surprising twist when the threat becomes a strength.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and build the SWOT for your own business idea.
